title: Abstract AST
description: Contract between the authoring layer (the Python builder) and the Rust runner. Version 0.2, 2026-09-30 (0.1 drafted the same day; 0.2 adds the container layout, unit and column handles, units/unit_index, and fadvise). Every node, expression, distribution, and handle is an object with exactly one key naming its kind (externally tagged). Sizes are byte integers, durations are nanosecond integers. Semantic rules the schema cannot express are listed in schema/README.md and enforced by the validator.

ast.description: Schema version this document conforms to.

posix.description: The API the application this abstract was traced from issues the I/O of its `posix` names through (contract 0.7; `api` in 0.6, `backend` before). Absent: sync. A run uses it by default (`--posix`); a run under another API imposes another workload on the storage. Declared only with a `posix` name (V19). Not part of the op stream or the fingerprint.

cache.description: The application's cache mode on its `posix` names (contract 0.6): `direct` when it opens every regular file O_DIRECT; absent: `per-open`, the open flags of the op stream. Not `direct` under posix `mmap`. A run uses it by default (`--cache`); another is another workload. Declared only with a `posix` name (V19). Not part of the op stream or the fingerprint.

s3.description: How the application's S3 client uses the store for its `s3` names (contract 0.7): `blocking`, a thread waiting on each request, or `async`, many requests in flight per thread. Absent: blocking. A run uses it by default (`--s3`); another is another workload. Declared only with an `s3` name; with `posix` names too, `async` goes with posix `io_uring` or `libaio` and `blocking` with the others (V19). Not part of the op stream or the fingerprint.

params.description: Named parameters, overridable from the CLI. `gpus` is reserved: the runner sets it from --gpus. A name has no dot (`ident`), so no parameter takes the name of a runner fact or result (`fact.…`, `result.…`; contract 0.11).

expect.description: Errnos the op may return; counted per site, not fatal. Any other error is a run failure. Not part of the fingerprint.

literal.description: A JSON scalar. null is the `none` outcome of a mixture.

param.description: A parameter (contract 0.11: a `default`, or, required, a `kind` and no default). A required parameter has no value until a use case, a submission, or the command line gives one; the runner refuses a run without it.

kind.description: A required parameter's kind (contract 0.11): what a value given for it must be; an `int` takes an integral number. A parameter with a default takes the default's kind.

scale.description: What a submission sizes per site (`samples`; contract 0.11): a benchmark's rules file freezes every `scale` parameter to required.

unit.description: Documentation only; values are already in canonical units.

value.description: A parameter value: a scalar, a distribution, or an array of these (a parameter array, indexed by a loop index).

dist.description: A distribution literal. Draws are positional: hash(seed, actor, site, loop indices).

uniform64.description: A 64-bit identifier; used for fresh conversation ids and the like.

empirical.description: Values with relative weights; lengths must match.

zipf.description: Over the ids of the dataset it is applied to, rank order fixed by the dataset seed.

hotset.description: With probability `weight`, uniform over the first `fraction` of ids (by the dataset seed's rank order); otherwise uniform over the rest.

mixture.description: Pick an arm by weight, then draw from it; a null arm yields none.

distref.description: A distribution, or an expression that evaluates to one (a parameter, or a cond selecting between distributions).

expr.description: A scalar-valued expression, evaluated positionally. Integer arithmetic; div is floor division.

index.description: The value of an enclosing loop or parallel index.

ref.description: The value of a let binding in scope.

at.description: The value binding `ref` takes at another index of its enclosing loop. On a binding of the same loop body (itself included) the index must be {sub: [{index: i}, e]} with e provably >= 1: a literal, a draw or parameter whose distribution has that minimum, or `add` of such a term and one provably >= 0 (a `mod`, a loop index, a literal, a draw with minimum >= 0); rule V3, contract 0.5. A required parameter qualifies on the document and its value is judged when given (contract 0.13).

actor.description: This actor's global id, or the number of instances of its template.

draw.description: A positional draw; its site is the node's structural path.

elem.description: Element of a parameter array, or of an `array` in scope (contract 0.15).

len.description: Length of a parameter array, or of an `array` in scope (contract 0.15).

sum.description: Sum of a numeric parameter array.

size.description: Bytes of a file, sample, region, chunk, or namespace object, from its definition.

offset.description: Byte offset of a sample or region inside its file.

unit_index.description: Index, within its file, of the unit (row group, record batch, chunk) holding a sample; or a unit handle's own index.

units.description: Number of units in a file (of a file, sample, or unit handle).

chunks.description: Number of chunk objects a `chunk`-realized file has.

dirs.description: Number of directories a dataset's pattern generates.

cond.description: Expression-level conditional; arms may be expressions, distributions, or handles.

published.description: The number of entries the named timeline holds before this step in one group, in planned order (contract 0.15, rule V30): a timeline's name for its group 0, or `{timeline, group}` (contract 0.17), `group` an integer. Not positional: `@` may not reach it.

entry.description: Value `key` of entry `index` of the named timeline in group `group` (contract 0.17; 0 when absent), in planned order; `index` below that group's `published` (contract 0.15, rule V30). Not positional: `@` may not reach it.

prev.description: The value the `let` `ref`, bound directly in a loop's body, took in the previous iteration of that loop under the same outer indices; `init` in the loop's first iteration. The same as `ref @ (i - step)` for a positional binding, read rather than recomputed, so it carries a value that depends on a timeline (contract 0.15, rule V31). `@` may not reach it.

fresh.description: A `seq` of this many new blocks (contract 0.16, rule V33): their origin is this node's position, keyed as a draw is (seed, actor, site, enclosing indices), so they are new at every position and the same when `@` recomputes them.

shared.description: A `seq` of the first `n` blocks of the shared prefix `id` (an integer): the same blocks in every lane, actor, and run (contract 0.16), as a system prompt is every session's.

prefix.description: The first blocks of a `seq`: `[seq, k]`, `0 <= k <= seq_len` (contract 0.16).

chunk_key.description: The key of whole chunk `chunk` (from 0) of `per` blocks of a `seq`, a non-negative integer: the chained hash of every block to the chunk's end (runner/REFERENCE.md §2), so two sequences give one key exactly when they hold the same blocks up to it (contract 0.16).

now.description: This lane's planned time in nanoseconds (contract 0.18, rule V30): only in a timeline, and not positional (`@` and `prev` may not reach it).

cached.description: An attribute of the entry a tier's `order` is computed for (contract 0.18, rule V33), only there: `stored`, `touched`, `freed` the tier's event counts when it was stored, last looked up, and last released (`stored` until then); `hits` the lookups that found it; `pos` its index in the sequence of the lookup that last found or stored it; `size` its size in the tier's unit.

tier.description: What a tier holds, read by its timed eviction's `when` and `count` (contract 0.19, rule V33), only there: `used` its entries' size in the tier's unit, `entries` how many it holds.

victim.description: The key of the entry an `on_evict` body runs for (contract 0.19, rule V35), only in that body.

handle.description: A reference to a file, directory, sample, region, or workload-created object. Names are computed, never stored.

ref.description: A let binding holding a handle.

file.description: A dataset file by id, or the file (or chunk object) that holds a sample handle.

dir.description: The id-th directory of a dataset's pattern.

object.description: A workload-created object, named by filling the namespace pattern's fields.

inventory.description: The inventory of the named dataset (contract 0.9): the one file its `inventory` declares in its root, of size `count × entry`.

consume.description: Next sample of a dataset without replacement: perm(position), position = actor + count * (b * B + j) over the enclosing loader and loop.

pick.description: A sample of a dataset with replacement, uniform unless a distribution over ids is given.

unit.description: A unit of a container file: unit `index` of the file `of` (a file or sample handle); without `index`, the unit holding the sample `of`. `offset` and `size` of it are the unit's extent, framing included.

column.description: Column chunk `index` of a unit (`of` a unit or sample handle). `offset` and `size` of it are the chunk's extent.

pattern.description: A path pattern with {field[:format]} fields, `{field div N}` or `{field mod N}` with N a positive number or (contract 0.10) the name of an integer parameter (V23). Datasets use `id` (and `k` for chunks); namespaces declare their fields.
Names of the dataset's files or objects: `{id}` (and `{k}`, the chunk, under `chunked`); an `array`'s one file, with no fields.

layout.description: How a unit of storage (a file or an object) holds the items (contract 0.8): `whole`, one item; `chunked`, part of one (`chunk` bytes a unit, named by `{k}`); `compound`, several variably sized items (`samples_per_file`, framed by `format`); `array`, `count` fixed-size slots in one file (`slot` bytes each). V20.

access.description: How the application finds the items (contract 0.8): `map`, samples drawn from the positional shuffle and read by offset; `stream`, files (shards) drawn from it and read sequentially; `indexed`, looked up by id (`file`, `pick`), never consumed. An `array` is `indexed`; a consumed dataset's directories are `{id div D}` or none (V21); the format class says which it supports (V9).

count.description: Number of items: samples, or an array's slots.

size.description: Bytes per item, drawn from the dataset seed; an array's capped at `slot`, the slot's tail unwritten.

samples_per_file.description: Samples in each file of a `compound` dataset (the last may hold fewer).

chunk.description: Realize each file as ceil(size / chunk) block objects named by the pattern's {k}.

slot.description: Slot c of an `array` starts at c * slot.

framing.description: The container framing (v0.2; `layout` until 0.8): file = file_header ‖ units ‖ file_footer, aligned; unit = unit_header ‖ column chunks ‖ unit_footer, aligned; column chunk = header ‖ rows, aligned; row = row_header ‖ fixed ‖ share of the sample ‖ row_footer, aligned. Every field is an expression over parameters; absent means 0 (alignments 1). No framing is the packed framing: samples back to back.

unit.description: Samples per unit (row group, record batch, chunk); default samples_per_file.

header.description: Bytes before the rows of this column chunk (a page header).

fixed.description: Bytes per row that do not come from the sample (an int64 label, an offset entry).

weight.description: Share of each sample's bytes this column carries; weights sum to 1; the last positive one takes the remainder.

row_align.description: Each row is padded to a multiple of this (default 1).

align.description: The column chunk is padded to a multiple of this (default 1).

columns.description: The column chunks of a unit; default one column of weight 1.

writer.description: Class-specific writer settings, opaque to the runner; part of the resolved definition the manifest compares.

format.description: Which format class wrote the container, and its layout. The layout is what the runner computes offsets from; the class, reader, version, and writer settings are matched against the manifest.

name.description: The file's name, directly in the dataset's root: a constant, not beginning with `.aeiou`, not a name the pattern can produce there (V22).

entry.description: Bytes per item of `count`: the inventory's size is `count × entry`.

inventory.description: A file list of the dataset (contract 0.9), written by datagen as payload and read through the `inventory` handle in place of a walk. Only a consumed dataset (`map` or `stream`) has one (V22). Under `run --subset` its reads are issued no further than its size at the run's count.

namespace.description: Workload-created objects: no count, no manifest entry; the directory must exist and be writable.

size.description: Bytes per object as an expression over the pattern's fields and parameters, or "as_written": the sum of the write lengths in the sequence that creates the object, computable at the creator's position. Never observed with fstat.

seed.description: Content of an object is a function of (seed, hash(path), offset).

input.description: The objects were written by a previous run (its `.aeiou-namespace.json` is required at the root) and this abstract only reads them: no write-mode op may target the namespace, and namespaces sharing its root must also be inputs (V14).

same_run.description: Only with `input`: the names this abstract reads are positional draws of the run that wrote them, so the run is refused unless its seed, its instance count, and every parameter both abstracts declare equal the writer's, as recorded in `.aeiou-namespace.json` (V15, contract 0.4).

count.description: Instances of this template, with global ids 0..count.

node.description: One statement. Ops (eighteen, with fadvise) are POSIX-shaped and identical for every backend.

let.description: Bind a name to a positional value or a handle; visible for the rest of the enclosing body and in child bodies.

loop.description: for index in [from, to) step `step`. The index is part of every RNG key inside.

join.description: False: the parent goes on at once and the sub-actors end with the enclosing timeline at the latest; only inside a `timeline` (contract 0.15, rule V30).

parallel.description: `width` concurrent sub-actors, index 0..width, joined at the end (unless `join` is false, inside a timeline).

channel.description: Declare a bounded channel in the enclosing actor.

put.description: Deliver item `seq`; blocks while the channel is full.

take.description: Wait for the next item (in sequence order on an ordered channel).

index.description: The batch index bound in the body.

loader.description: PyTorch-style sugar the runner keeps: `workers` sub-actors, worker w builds batches w, w+W, ...; an ordered channel of workers*prefetch slots named `name`; exactly `batches` batches. Deferred: records-per-batch for stream access.

cond.description: Statement conditional; the test may use only loop indices, parameters, bindings, and the actor id.

choose.description: Run one arm, chosen positionally by weight (the selection construct).

phase.description: Statistics label for every op inside; no effect on execution or the fingerprint.

trace.description: A captured trace of a real application, executed literally, for small-scale calibration; never CLOSED. `file` is relative to the document. Deferred: the trace file format (renamed from `replay` 2026-10-02).

offset.description: Positioned read (pread); absent means sequential from the current file position.

repeat.description: until_eof: reads of `len` until the known size is exhausted, including the terminating short or zero-length read; each returned count is checked against the computed size.

len.description: 0: to the end of the file.

fadvise.description: posix_fadvise on an open file. WILLNEED starts readahead on NFS, which is why pyarrow's reads are modeled with it (added 2026-09-30).

truncate.description: `truncate(2)` of a path, open or not (contract 0.14, DESIGN_REVIEW.md §3.92): the file's size set to `len`. A changing op: never on a dataset (V12) or an input namespace (V14), never on a namespace in an object store (V18).

mode.description: `fallocate(2)`'s mode flags (contract 0.14, DESIGN_REVIEW.md §3.92). Absent or empty: mode 0, allocate and extend. `KEEP_SIZE` allocates past the end without extending; `PUNCH_HOLE` (only with `KEEP_SIZE`) frees the range; `ZERO_RANGE`, `COLLAPSE_RANGE`, `INSERT_RANGE`, `UNSHARE_RANGE`, `WRITE_ZEROES` as Linux defines them. At most one operation besides `KEEP_SIZE`, which `COLLAPSE_RANGE`, `INSERT_RANGE`, and `WRITE_ZEROES` do not take (V29). Part of the op and of the fingerprint.

readdir.description: getdents64 until exhausted, on a handle opened with DIRECTORY.

caches.description: The timeline's caches (contract 0.16, rule V33): their state walked in planned order with the lanes, empty when the timeline starts.

resources.description: The timeline's counted resources (contract 0.18, rule V34), none held when it starts.

timeline.description: Lanes planned together (contract 0.15, DESIGN_REVIEW.md §3.99, rule V30): the body's main line and every sub-actor of a `parallel` in it is a lane with a planned clock, which a `compute` moves by `ns`. The lane planned soonest takes the next step, a tie going to the smaller lane key; a lane runs until its next `compute`. Never a `timeline`, `channel`, `put`, `take`, `loader`, `barrier`, or `trace` inside. Its `caches` (contract 0.16, rule V33) and `resources` (contract 0.18, rule V34) are walked with its lanes, in planned order; a lane that must wait for one is parked until a release, and resumes at the release's planned time. `aeiou run` does not run one yet.

publish.description: An entry of the enclosing timeline: these values at this lane's planned time, in group `group` (contract 0.17, an integer; 0 when absent), which the other lanes read with `published` and `entry` of that group (contract 0.15, rule V30).

array.description: `count` values computed once, where the node stands, each with `index` bound as a loop index (so its draws are positional), read with `elem` and `len` as a parameter array is; never inside a loop, never the name of a parameter (contract 0.15, rule V32).

lookup.description: The longest run of `seq`'s leading whole chunks of `per` blocks held in a tier of a cache of the enclosing timeline, bound to `bind` as an integer; then the chunks the tier holds touched, in order, and the others stored, in order (contract 0.18; 0.16 interleaved them), each `size` in a tier that counts bytes, exactly then. With `hold` (contract 0.18, rule V34), the chunks found and stored are held by this lane under that name until its `release`, never victims meanwhile. Not positional: `@` and `prev` may not reach `bind`.

acquire.description: `n` units of a resource of the enclosing timeline, held by this lane under `hold` until its `release` (contract 0.18, rule V34); the lane waits in planned time while they are not free or an earlier lane waits, first come first.

release.description: What this lane holds under `hold`, given back (contract 0.18, rule V34): a resource's units, or a tier's entries, which become victims again with `freed` the release. A lane ends holding nothing.

probe.description: The longest run of `seq`'s whole chunks of `per` blocks from chunk `from` held in a tier of a cache of the enclosing timeline, bound to `bind` as an integer; nothing changed (contract 0.19, rule V33). Not positional: `@` and `prev` may not reach `bind`.

touch.description: The chunks `from` to `from + count` (cut at the sequence's end), or those whose indices the array `chunks` holds (an `array`, a `store`'s `taken`, or a parameter array; an index outside the sequence refused), that a tier holds, touched as one event: `touched` the same for all, `pos` each chunk's index; the others ignored (contract 0.19, rule V33). `from` and `count` together, or `chunks` alone.

store.description: The chunks `from` to `from + count` (cut at the sequence's end), or those whose indices the array `chunks` holds (an `array`, a `store`'s `taken`, or a parameter array; an index outside the sequence refused), that a tier lacks, stored as one event, each `size` in a tier that counts bytes, exactly then; those it holds left as they are, or, with `present: renew`, stored again as if absent (a new entry; a chunk a lane holds is left as it is). A tier with timed eviction makes no room at store, so a chunk past its capacity is what `full` says (`skip`: a planned drop). With `bind`, the leading run of the range held after it; with `taken`, an array of the indices of the chunks it stored, in the order acted on, read with `len` and `elem` after the store (contract 0.19, rule V33; not the name of a parameter, V32); not on a tier whose `full` is `wait`. `from` and `count` together, or `chunks` alone. Not positional: `@` and `prev` may not reach `bind`.

ast_sha256.description: Hash of the canonical form with this block removed.

protocol.description: Where a dataset or namespace lives (contract 0.6; `s3` was `object` until 0.7): a file system (`posix`, absent) or an S3 store (`s3`), each run giving it an endpoint (`--endpoint NAME=DIR`, default under `--root`, or `--endpoint NAME=s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX]`, required for `s3`). Not part of the dataset id or the namespace's resolved definition; datasets and namespaces sharing a root declare the same protocol (V17). The runner reaches an `s3` name through its object engine (cargo feature `object`); an `s3` namespace is written once, in order, per object (V18).

source.description: A value the storage reports (contract 0.11, DESIGN_REVIEW.md §3.78 point 11): `st_blksize`, read before the gate by `stat` of the first file of dataset `of` or (contract 0.12) of namespace `of`: the first object its manifest lists for an input namespace (the manifest where it lists none), a probe file created and removed in its root for an output one (`aeiou dry-run --st-blksize` in place of the storage), `fallback` where the storage reports none (an object store). The system under test's by the interposition test: the workload id covers the rule, the report the number. Rule V28.

cache.description: A cache of a timeline (contract 0.16, brief item 75): its tiers by name.

order.description: The victim order (contract 0.18): integer expressions over `cached` and parameters, computed for an entry when it is stored, looked up, or released and kept; the entry whose values are least, compared in turn, is evicted first, a tie to the entry stored first. Absent, nothing is evicted. Needs a `capacity`.

full.description: What a store does when the tier has no room and no victim left (contract 0.18): `skip` (the default) leaves the entry out; `wait` holds the lane, in planned time, until a release makes room for the whole lookup, first come first; `fail` refuses the walk. `wait` and `fail` need a `capacity`.

evict.description: Timed eviction (contract 0.19, rule V33): at every planned instant k × `every` ns from the timeline's start, while lanes remain and before any lane's step at that instant, if `when` holds, the `count` entries least in `order` that no lane holds are evicted; never at store. `when` and `count` read parameters, literals, and `tier`; `every` parameters and literals. Needs a `capacity` and an `order`; not with `full` `wait`.

on_evict.description: What each victim runs (contract 0.19, rule V35): `body`, with `victim` its key, on eviction lanes of the timeline, victim i of a batch on lane i mod `lanes`, at the planned instant of the tick or the store that evicted it, before any other lane's step at that instant. The body sees the bindings around the timeline and parameters; it holds no `compute`, `lookup`, `probe`, `touch`, `store`, `acquire`, `release`, `publish`, `parallel`, `loader`, channel, barrier, timeline, or trace. `lanes` reads parameters and literals. Needs an `order`.

tier.description: A tier (contracts 0.16, 0.18, and 0.19, rule V33): at most `capacity` (counted in entries, the default, or bytes) of entries no lane holds evicted by `order`, at store or, with `evict`, at planned ticks; held entries are never victims; an entry larger than the tier is not stored.

resource.description: A counted resource of a timeline (contract 0.18, rule V34): `capacity` units, held by `acquire` and given back by `release`; a queue with `capacity` servers.
